name: Dabyrie's Farmstead
summary: In northern Arathi, the Dabyries keep their farm against the dangers around them. Kenata Dabyrie holds fast with her sons, loyal to Stromgarde and the Alliance in a realm broken by the Third War.

sections.title: A Bastion in the Highlands
sections.body: Kenata Dabyrie and her sons hold their farm against the dangers around them. Fardel and Marcel work the fields while a local family militia guards the grounds. Few human homesteads still endure in the broken kingdom of Stromgarde. Aggressive wildlife and bandits threaten the farm, and the Forsaken press from the north. The Dabyries keep their home in a land where few human settlements remain.

sections.title: Bitter Feuds
sections.body: The Forsaken have turned against the Dabyries, and Genavie Callow is among their bitterest foes. Once a noblewoman, Callow lost her lands and kin during the Third War. She accuses the surviving Dabyrie family of taking her family's heirlooms amid the plague's chaos. Now Horde mercenaries target the modest farm to settle old grudges from the north.

faq.answer: Kenata Dabyrie lives at the farm with her sons, Fardel and Marcel. They are human citizens of Stromgarde, loyal to the Alliance and defended by a sworn local militia.

faq.q: Why is the Horde targeting this farm?
faq.answer: The Forsaken woman Genavie Callow holds a grudge against the Dabyries. She accuses them of taking her family's estate and surviving heirlooms while her relatives perished in the Third War.

faq.q: Is Dabyrie's Farmstead part of Stromgarde?
faq.answer: Yes. The Dabyries consider themselves subjects of Stromgarde and allies of the broader Alliance, though their capital lies in ruins to the south.
Highland predators and roaming Syndicate cutthroats threaten the farm. Forsaken forces press from the north.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you can find a rare reminder here that Stromgarde's people still survive and fight for their land amid encroaching enemies.
As Forsaken, you see a prosperous human farm holding goods your people say were taken from families who perished during the Third War.
